questions.question: How is $\dim(V)$ defined for a finite-dimensional vector space $V$?
options: As the number of zero vectors in $V$.
As the number of all vectors in $V$.
As the length of any basis of $V$.
As the length of the longest vector in $V$.

questions.question: Why does dimension count “independent directions”?
options: It measures the Euclidean length of basis vectors.
A basis gives the independent directions needed to describe every vector.
It counts all possible scalar coefficients in the field, in every case without exception.
It counts every vector in the space one by one.

questions.question: Why is the definition of dimension independent of the chosen basis?
options: All bases contain exactly the same vectors, regardless of the specific input chosen.
Any two bases of a finite-dimensional vector space have the same length.
Only the standard basis is allowed.

questions.question: What is the dimension of $\mathbb R^n$?
options: It depends on the vector chosen.

questions.question: Why is the length of a redundant spanning list not necessarily the dimension?
options: Dimension counts every vector in the vector space.
Dimension uses a basis, not an arbitrary spanning list.

questions.question: What is $\dim(\mathbb R^2)$?
options: Infinitely many, because $\mathbb R^2$ has infinitely many vectors.
